description: We’re a team of student builders from Doha, Qatar, who love turning data into tools people can actually use. We combine AI, software, and hardware to tackle real problems, and we’re excited to dig into NASA’s open data and explore what it can reveal about life and safety beyond Earth. Curious, hands-on, and always learning.
summary:
1gnition is an evidence navigator for NASA microgravity fire data, built for the Space Apps 2026 “Flame in Freefall” challenge. In space, flames don’t rise, so results from fire tests on Earth don’t carry over. NASA’s PSI archive holds the flight data, but it’s hard to tell which runs apply to a new scenario, which comparisons are fair and where the data runs out.

Users set a scenario: material, oxygen, pressure, gravity and airflow. 1gnition ranks the indexed Saffire investigations by relevance and by how closely their conditions match the scenario. Compare Runs shows whether two runs differ in only one condition or in several at once, which makes the comparison unfair. The Scale Transfer Lab presents three published comparisons from Olson et al. (2023). It keeps flame length (cm) separate from spread rate (cm/s) and shows which conditions matched, changed, are unknown or conflict. Research Gaps shows that a lunar habitat’s atmosphere falls outside every tested run, and it proposes the experiment that is missing.

Every number links to its source, page and read method. Where sources disagree, 1gnition shows the conflict instead of picking one value. NASA-data prediction isn’t validated yet, so 1gnition shows no predicted rate and no accuracy score. Synthetic test data is clearly marked as not NASA data. Ask 1gnition is an offline, rule-based helper that answers only from the indexed records.

Zero guessing. Zero hidden uncertainty.
details:
1gnition shows what NASA’s microgravity fire data can and can’t support. Users set a scenario: material, oxygen, pressure, gravity and airflow. 1gnition then ranks the Saffire investigations from NASA’s PSI archive by relevance and by how closely their conditions match. Compare Runs shows whether two runs differ in only one condition or in several at once, which makes the comparison unfair. The Scale Transfer Lab presents three published comparisons from Olson et al. (2023) and keeps flame length (cm) separate from spread rate (cm/s). Research Gaps shows where a lunar habitat’s atmosphere falls outside every tested run and proposes the missing experiment.

Impact: fire safety on the Moon and Mars depends on knowing where the evidence ends. 1gnition stops people from over-reading single runs and points researchers to the tests that are still needed.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no framework; Python for the data pipeline, ML package and API server; JSON data; Playwright and GitHub Actions for automated testing; GitHub Pages for hosting.

Creativity: 1gnition is built to refuse to guess. The ML backend reports that its predictions aren’t validated, so the site shows no predicted rate or accuracy score, and synthetic test data is clearly labelled.

Factors considered: every number links to its source and page, conflicting sources are shown openly, units are never mixed, and labels say how strong each piece of evidence is.
